summary: Resolved the tie-break anomaly and turned it into a distinct, sourced defect. The recorded state is now explained end to end: a prepare reply from a replica that holds the instance with no command carries a nil command slice, the decoder allocates it with make([]state.Command, alen1) so the receiver sees a non-nil empty slice (epaxos/defs.go:228-235), the adoption loop copies that empty slice into lb.cmds because its value ballot equals the running candidate ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246), and the sub-case 5/6 fallback substitutes state.NOOP() only when lb.cmds is nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311) - which an empty slice is not - so startPhase1 is called with an empty command batch and the owner's own instance ends PREACCEPTED with a zero-length command list (receipt 81a44ff62122417db3cc5697fc5303f6, indices 0, 3, 4, 5 and 9-11; both declared comparisons violated with witnesses 5 and 11). Consequences derived from source: the instance is proposed and can be decided with no command at all, replacing the command its own owner held; executeCommands accepts the empty non-nil batch because its guard is a nil test, so it executes as a no-op instead of stalling; and the client re-offer that protects the fabricated-NOOP case does not fire here because handleCommit tests for exactly one command with operation NONE (epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1099). I also corrected my own earlier statements: the order-independence claim is withdrawn as untested (the probe never applied its order parameter), and the status/command invariant entry is qualified rather than wrong, since this path reaches a status-without-command state through an empty non-nil slice that its nil test does not cover. Both open gaps of the question are answered as resolved, the new behavior entry records the decode-and-fallback pair with its receipt, and the run now holds six explained questions, four asserted defects each grounded in retained receipts, one holds account and nine evidence-linked knowledge entries.
